title: Vitest Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Vitest. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: What is the expected total?
questions.explanation: Vitest runs named tests and reports mismatched expectations. It works with JavaScript and TypeScript projects. This test passes because the total is 5.

questions.question: Which coordinate holds 4?
questions.explanation: toEqual compares the values inside an object. It is useful when a function returns a new object. The test passes because both coordinates match.

questions.question: Which field is checked?
questions.explanation: objectContaining checks selected fields when other fields are not part of the current test. The title is checked. The pages field is allowed but not checked by this expectation.

questions.question: How many cases run here?
questions.explanation: test.each repeats one rule for a table of examples. This reduces repeated test code while keeping cases visible. Three square-number cases run.

questions.question: Why recreate names?
options: To make every test use more memory forever
To give each test fresh data
questions.explanation: A fixture is prepared data used by a test. beforeEach can give each test a new fixture. The list starts with one learner for each test.

questions.question: Which value was passed to notify?
questions.explanation: vi.fn creates a spy that records its calls. You can check the arguments as well as the count. The call with 7 is recorded.

questions.question: Which action restores original methods?
questions.explanation: vi.spyOn watches an existing method. Restore it after the test so later code sees the normal method again. The spied method returns 9 during the test. Cleanup restores the original method.

questions.question: Why use await?
questions.explanation: Use await when checking a promise. The test must stay active until the check is finished. The promise resolves to ready, so the test passes.

questions.question: Is this rejection expected?
options: No, every rejection is a test bug
questions.explanation: A failing promise can be the correct result for invalid input. rejects tests that case explicitly. The test passes when the promise rejects with the expected error.

questions.question: What triggers the reminder here?
questions.explanation: Vitest can replace timers with a controlled clock. This makes a timer test quick and repeatable. The fake clock reaches 500 milliseconds and triggers the reminder once.

questions.question: What does this test require?
questions.explanation: A Node test has no real browser page. Choose a DOM test environment or browser mode when the behaviour needs page elements. With a DOM environment configured, the test creates a button and checks its text.

questions.question: What does coverage measure?
options: Whether every possible bug is gone
questions.explanation: Coverage reports which code was reached by tests. Reaching a line does not prove its result was checked well. Both checks state a result. A coverage report is useful alongside these expectations.
